boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented ways Montclair State marks Red Hawk pride, mascot milestones and shared campus moments.

cards.title: Make “The Hawk”
cards.subtitle: Montclair’s ASL-for-hawk pride sign
cards.notes: Learn the American Sign Language sign for “hawk,” then use it to show Red Hawk pride at campus activities and events.
cards.short_summary: A Montclair-created hand sign rooted in the ASL sign for “hawk.”
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Homecoming page identifies “The Hawk” Gesture as a school tradition created using the ASL sign for “hawk.”
cards.access_notes: Use at campus activities or events.

cards.title: High-five Rocky at Homecoming
cards.subtitle: A mascot-photo moment during the celebration
cards.notes: Look for Rocky the Red Hawk during Homecoming, offer a high-five and take a photo to mark the day with the mascot.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming makes Rocky photo opportunities part of Red Hawk pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Homecoming page encourages attendees to high-five Rocky and take a picture with him during Homecoming.
cards.access_notes: Available when Rocky appears at Homecoming.

cards.title: Know the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: “All hail to thee Montclair”
cards.notes: Read through the Alma Mater before Homecoming so you can recognize its refrain and join the university’s shared song.
cards.short_summary: Montclair publishes the Alma Mater as part of its traditions guide.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Homecoming traditions page presents the university’s Alma Mater, including its refrain.
cards.access_notes: The lyrics are publicly posted online.

cards.title: Wear your Montclair colors
cards.subtitle: Scarlet-and-white school-spirit apparel
cards.notes: Bring a Montclair hat, shirt, hoodie or other item to Homecoming if you want to visibly take part in Red Hawk pride.
cards.short_summary: The university lists wearing Montclair gear among its Homecoming pride traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Homecoming page calls wearing Montclair gear one of the ways to show school pride.
cards.access_notes: Existing apparel can be used; the page also identifies the Student Center Bookstore.

cards.title: Consider the Class Gift
cards.subtitle: A graduating-class giving tradition
cards.notes: If you are graduating and choose to participate, direct your Class Gift to a Montclair area you care about, such as a fund or program.
cards.short_summary: Graduating classes are invited to support areas of the university that matter to them.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair describes an annual Class Gift tradition in which graduating students support university areas important to them.
cards.access_notes: Optional and intended for graduating students.

cards.title: Wear red on Friday
cards.subtitle: A weekly Red Hawk pride cue
cards.notes: Choose a red item on Fridays to join the university’s plainly stated school-spirit practice; no special location or registration is needed.
cards.short_summary: A simple weekly way Montclair signals Red Hawk pride.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s Pride and Traditions page states, “On Fridays We Wear Red!”
cards.source_title: Pride and Traditions | Red Hawk Life
cards.access_notes: Wear any red item on Friday.

cards.entity_name: Rub the Red Hawk Statue’s Beak
cards.title: Rub the beak for luck
cards.subtitle: A finals and game-day Red Hawk ritual
cards.notes: Visit the bronze Red Hawk statue before finals or a game day and rub its beak, following the university’s documented good-luck custom.
cards.short_summary: The 12-foot Red Hawk statue anchors a luck ritual tied to finals and game days.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair instructs students to rub the Red Hawk statue’s beak for good luck during finals and on game days.
cards.source_title: Pride and Traditions | Red Hawk Life
cards.access_notes: The statue is on the Montclair campus; be considerate of others taking photos.

cards.entity_name: Rocky the Red Hawk Birthday Party
cards.title: Celebrate Rocky’s birthday
cards.subtitle: An annual mascot birthday tradition
cards.notes: Watch campus event listings near Rocky’s October 5 birthday and join the birthday celebration if it is offered during your visit.
cards.short_summary: Rocky’s birthday party has been an annual campus tradition since its first 2017 celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s mascot history says Rocky first celebrated his birthday in 2017 and that the party is now an annual campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Rocky was hatched on October 5; verify the year’s event details before attending.

cards.title: Mark Pebbles’ November birthday
cards.subtitle: An annual Student Recreation Center event
cards.notes: Check November campus programming for Pebbles’ birthday celebration, which grew from her first birthday event into an annual gathering.
cards.short_summary: Montclair’s pupscot has a recurring November birthday event.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair says Pebbles’ birthday celebration became an annual campus event held each November at the Student Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: Verify the annual event listing and time before going.

cards.title: Catch the Puppy Parade
cards.subtitle: A February Gotcha Day tradition across the Quad
cards.notes: Look for Pebbles’ February Gotcha Day programming and the Puppy Parade across the Quad; confirm the event listing before planning around it.
cards.short_summary: Pebbles’ adoption anniversary includes a recurring February parade.
cards.evidence_claim: Montclair’s mascot history says Pebbles’ Gotcha Day includes an inaugural Puppy Parade across the Quad, a tradition that continues each February.
cards.access_notes: Held in connection with February Gotcha Day programming; verify current details.
